skill.name: frontend-slides
skill.description: Create responsive, animation-rich HTML presentations from notes, images, or PowerPoint files.
skill.summary: Build single-file HTML slide decks with responsive layouts, motion, and optional PPTX conversion.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most high and medium static findings are false positives from Markdown inline code, CSS examples, and JavaScript property names. The real issues are operational: PPTX conversion can run Python and pip, browser opening invokes an OS command, and generated decks may load third-party fonts. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or malicious behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Command execution during PPT conversion and delivery
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running Python, pip install, or OS open commands. Prefer argument arrays and trusted local script paths.

remediation.issue: Third-party font loading in generated presentations
remediation.suggestion: Document that generated HTML may request external font CSS. Provide an offline font option for sensitive or air-gapped presentations.

content.value_statement: Building polished slide decks in HTML can be slow and easy to break across viewports. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create responsive, animated presentations from notes or PPTX files.
actual_capabilities: Creates self-contained HTML presentations with inline CSS and JavaScript.
Generates three visual style previews before building the final deck.
Extracts text, images, and notes from PPTX files using a helper script.
Applies viewport fitting rules for desktop, tablet, and phone screens.
Adds keyboard navigation, touch navigation, progress bars, and slide dots.
Supports optional in-browser text editing with local save and export controls.
limitations: PPTX conversion needs Python and the python-pptx package.
Generated decks may load external web fonts unless changed.
Complex PowerPoint transitions and proprietary effects may not convert exactly.
Very dense source material may need manual slide splitting.

use_cases.title: Build a Pitch Deck
use_cases.description: Turn notes, goals, and brand direction into a polished HTML deck with motion and strong visual hierarchy.

use_cases.title: Convert Training Slides
use_cases.description: Extract content from an existing PPTX and rebuild it as a responsive browser presentation.

use_cases.title: Refresh Conference Material
use_cases.description: Improve an existing HTML deck with better typography, animation, navigation, and viewport fit.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Deck
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new presentation from rough notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a responsive HTML presentation about my topic. Ask for purpose, audience, length, and style before generating the deck.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a PPTX Deck
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request to turn PowerPoint content into HTML.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert my PPTX file into a browser-based HTML presentation. Extract the content, summarize the slides, then ask me to choose a style.

prompt_templates.title: Enhance Existing Slides
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request to improve a current HTML presentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this HTML presentation and improve its layout, typography, animations, and viewport fit while preserving the message.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a Branded Executive Deck
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with strict design and delivery requirements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a branded executive deck with three style previews, curated motion, optional inline editing, and clear speaker-ready slide structure.

output_examples.input: A founder asks for a ten-slide seed pitch deck from rough notes.
output_examples.output: The result is a single HTML presentation with a title slide, problem, solution, market, traction, team, and closing slides.

output_examples.input: A training team provides a PPTX with product onboarding material.
output_examples.output: The skill extracts slide text and images, asks for a style choice, then rebuilds the deck for browser viewing.

output_examples.input: A speaker wants an existing HTML deck to feel more polished.
output_examples.output: The deck receives stronger typography, cleaner navigation, reduced overflow risk, and motion that supports the talk.

best_practices: Provide audience, purpose, slide count, and source material before generation starts.
Review style previews before approving the full deck build.
Test the final deck at common presentation sizes before delivery.
anti_patterns: Do not cram long documents into a few slides.
Do not skip viewport checks after adding images or dense content.
Do not enable inline editing unless the deck needs live text changes.

faq.question: Can it create a presentation from scratch?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks discovery questions, proposes styles, and generates a complete responsive HTML slide deck.

faq.question: Can it convert PowerPoint files?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses a Python helper to extract PPTX text, images, and notes before rebuilding the deck.

faq.question: Does the output need a server?
faq.answer: No. The target output is a self-contained HTML file that opens in a browser.

faq.question: Can the deck work offline?
faq.answer: Mostly. External web fonts should be replaced with local fonts for fully offline use.

faq.question: Does it support live editing?
faq.answer: Yes. Inline editing is optional and can save changes locally before export.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: It suits teams that need polished browser presentations without a full frontend build system.
